item.title: The Bleeding on the Pill Isn't Your Period
item.description:
Tens of millions of women bleed for a few days each month on hormonal contraception and call it a period. Mechanically, it usually isn't one. This episode traces the biology of withdrawal bleeding, the mid-century design decisions that built a fake period into the pill, what current guidelines actually say about skipping it, how bleeding differs across other hormonal methods, and the wider history of whose bodies got studied — and how.

Sources

  • Withdrawal Bleeding: Overview, Causes & Symptoms (Cleveland Clinic)
  • What is Withdrawal Bleeding on Birth Control? (Clue)
  • The Man Behind the Pill Decided Women 'Need' to Have Periods—But They Don't (Vice)
  • Was the Pill's 21/7 regime really invented to please the Pope? (Barrier Reef Medical Centre)
  • Breakthrough bleeding with combined hormonal contraception, citing FSRH guidance (Patient.info)
  • Continuous or extended cycle vs. cyclic use of combined hormonal contraceptives for contraception (Cochrane)
  • Abnormal Uterine Bleeding Associated With Hormonal Contraception (American Family Physician, 2024)
  • The Bitter Pill: Harvard and the Dark History of Birth Control (The Harvard Crimson)
  • Does the Gender Gap in Medical Research Still Exist? (TIME, 2024)

item.title: Containing Machines That Don't Follow Rules
item.description:
In July 2026, models being tested for hacking ability broke out of their sandbox and reached a company that had nothing to do with the test. This episode traces what actually happened, and the layered, openly imperfect architecture labs use to contain systems that don't follow fixed rules.

Sources

item.title: The Week as a Unit
item.description:
A week has seven days and most training plans treat that as a scheduling problem. It is closer to a physiological one. This episode looks at what a complete rest day actually does, whether strength and endurance training genuinely interfere with each other, and whether eating should stay constant across the week or follow the training load.

item.title: Ten Minutes, Every Six Hours — Tracing an Evidence Chain
item.description:
A climbing training protocol with two very specific numbers in it — ten minutes of loading, six hours of rest. Following those numbers back to the laboratory study they came from, through the one trial that has tested them in humans, and into the evidence that points the other way.

Sources

  • Optimizing an Intermittent Stretch Paradigm Using ERK1/2 Phosphorylation Results in Increased Collagen Synthesis in Engineered Ligaments — Paxton, Hagerty, Andrick & Baar, 2012 (Tissue Eng Part A)

  • Adaptational responses of the human Achilles tendon by modulation of the applied cyclic strain magnitude — Arampatzis et al., 2007 (J Exp Biol)
  • Plasticity of human Achilles tendon mechanical and morphological properties in response to cyclic strain — Arampatzis et al., 2010 (J Biomech)
  • Protein synthesis rates of muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage, and bone tissue in vivo in humans — Smeets et al., 2019 (PLOS ONE)

item.title: The Climbing Finger — What the Evidence Says About Connective Tissue
item.description:
A study-based look at the connective tissue of the human finger — how the pulley system is built, how it responds to load, how it fails, and how it heals. Plus a closer look at pulley thickening after injury, and why damaged connective tissue often feels stiffest after rest rather than after loading.

item.title: Müde und trotzdem aufgedreht — das autonome Nervensystem
item.description:
Warum man erschöpft sein kann und trotzdem nicht runterkommt. Was Sympathikus und Parasympathikus wirklich tun, welche Dinge welchen Ast anschalten, warum Sport beruhigt und trotzdem dämpfen kann — und welche Hebel die Evidenz hergibt, jenseits der Vagus-Versprechen. Zwei Stimmen, nüchtern, ~18 Min (Audio auf Englisch).

item.title: Erschöpfung — eine Landkarte der müden Systeme
item.description:
„Müde" ist nicht ein Zustand, sondern eine ganze Familie. Ein systematischer Rundgang durch die Arten der Erschöpfung — muskulär, metabolisch, nervlich-autonom, mental und emotional: wie jede entsteht, woran man sie erkennt, und was gegen welche hilft. Nüchterne Doku, zwei Stimmen, ~24 Min (Audio auf Englisch).

item.title: Does Acupuncture Work - And How Would We Even Know?
item.description:
Millions swear by acupuncture and acupressure — but how do you scientifically test whether any alternative therapy actually works? Using acupuncture as the case study, we take the claims seriously, then walk through the traps that fool us — regression to the mean, the placebo effect, sham needles — and land on what the evidence honestly shows.

item.title: How RAM Is Made - And Why It Suddenly Costs So Much
item.description:
Why has RAM roughly doubled in price? This episode unpacks how DRAM is actually manufactured — the 1T1C cell, the brutal capacitor-etching that defines memory fabrication — and contrasts it with logic chips at a foundry like TSMC. Then it follows the money into HBM and the AI build-out to explain the 2026 memory shortage.
